answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a stake-and-slash rule: every agent locks a bond before voting, and peers who expose a duplicate trigger forfeiture. Because influence tracks locked collateral, splitting one wallet into a thousand puppets yields not a thousand votes but the same stake divided, so each fake voice counts for less. The attacker pays: to rival one honest agent he must lock equal capital, and one proven fraud burns the whole bond and blacklists his key. Whether pricing a walnut, mapping the tundra, or bidding on marble, every new identity demands forfeitable stake.
